Joshua “The Fearless” Van,                                    is a professional mixed martial artist from Myanmar who competes in the UFC’s flyweight division at 125 pounds. Born on October 10, 2001, Van has become one of the most exciting and talked-about fighters in mixed martial arts, rising from a young prospect to a UFC flyweight champion before even turning 25. He is known for his relentless striking, incredible pace, aggressive combinations, toughness, and willingness to stand in front of dangerous opponents and turn fights into absolute wars. His journey through MMA has been remarkable, and his achievements at such a young age have made him one of the most interesting fighters to follow in the entire UFC. Van’s journey began in Myanmar, where he was born and spent the early part of his childhood. His family later moved to Malaysia before immigrating to the United States in 2013. After settling in Houston, Texas, Van eventually found his way into mixed martial arts, developing the skills and competitive mindset that would eventually take him to the highest level of the sport. What started as a young man discovering a passion for fighting eventually became a professional career that would lead him into the UFC octagon, where he would compete against some of the best flyweights in the world. Van began his professional MMA career in 2021 and quickly started building experience through regional competition. He developed a reputation as an aggressive, high-output striker who could overwhelm opponents with combinations and maintain a demanding pace. He also demonstrated that he was capable of winning through different methods, including knockouts, technical knockouts, submissions, and decisions. His performances helped him earn a UFC contract, and he made his promotional debut on June 24, 2023, against Zhalgas Zhumagulov. Van won that fight by split decision, beginning his UFC career with a victory in a closely contested matchup. From there, Van continued working his way through the flyweight division. He defeated Kevin Borjas by unanimous decision at UFC 295, then stopped Felipe Bunes by second-round TKO in January 2024. He followed those performances with victories over Edgar Chairez and Cody Durden, establishing himself as a young fighter with the potential to become a serious contender. Although he suffered a third-round knockout loss to Charles Johnson in July 2024, Van did not allow that setback to define his career. He returned to competition, continued improving, and began putting together the victories that would eventually take him into championship contention. One of the defining characteristics of Joshua Van’s career has been his ability to bounce back from adversity. Losing is part of mixed martial arts, and even the best fighters experience setbacks. What separates fighters is how they respond. Van returned from his loss to Charles Johnson with renewed determination, defeating Rei Tsuruya by unanimous decision and stopping Bruno Silva by third-round TKO. He then earned an important unanimous-decision victory over Brandon Royval, an experienced and dangerous flyweight known for his unpredictable style and ability to create difficult situations for his opponents. Defeating someone of Royval’s calibre was a significant achievement and helped establish Van as a legitimate contender for the UFC flyweight championship. His rise continued when he faced Alexandre Pantoja for the UFC flyweight title at UFC 323 in December 2025. The fight ended after just 26 seconds when Pantoja suffered an arm injury, resulting in a TKO victory for Van. With that win, Joshua Van became the UFC flyweight champion, achieving something that most professional fighters spend their entire careers chasing. Although the unusual circumstances of the fight meant that some fans wanted to see the two men compete again, Van had officially reached the top of the division at just 24 years old.
